_: THE TEN-YEAR MASTER PLAN — every assumption, in one auditable file.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND WHAT IT IS NOT
scripts/publication/masterplan.mjs computes the entire ten-year
model from this file and from the VERIFIED commercial and academic
records already held in data/tuition.json and data/commercial.json.
Nothing in the model is typed twice and nothing is typed into a
page. If a figure in the published plan cannot be traced to this
file or to those two, tests/masterplan.test.mjs fails the build.
THE DISTINCTION THIS FILE TURNS ON, and it is the whole of its
integrity: every quantity below is classified. `verified` means the
College has adopted it and it is published. `assumption` means this
plan asserts it for the purpose of modelling and it has not been
adopted. `board` means it requires a decision nobody has taken.
A plan that blurs those three is not a plan; it is a wish with a
table in it.
THE ARCHITECTURE CONFLICT, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED QUIETLY
The commissioning brief for this plan carried a different academic
and commercial architecture from the one the College has adopted:
ten levels of 120 hours at $7,400 (directed) or $14,800 (tutored),
against the adopted six levels of 200 hours at $19,000. The two
agree on one figure only — 1,200 total academic hours.
The model is built on the ADOPTED architecture, because that is
what data/tuition.json holds, what tests/commercial-model.test.mjs
enforces, and what /admissions/tuition/ publishes to the public. A
ten-year plan whose base price contradicts the College's own
published fee schedule is not a plan anybody can act on.
The brief's architecture is not discarded. It is modelled in full
as ALTERNATIVE ARCHITECTURE A, with its financial and academic
effect computed rather than asserted, in the plan's Three Architectures section.

verified_basis._: Read from data/tuition.json and data/commercial.json at build time. Listed here only so a reader knows what the model treats as given. The engine never copies these numbers; it imports them.

_: FOUR MARKETS, ENTERED IN SEQUENCE RATHER THAN AT ONCE.
An institution with one campus, one platform and a finite number
of instructors cannot open four markets in its first year and
serve any of them well. The sequence below is a strategic choice:
the College earns its reputation where the qualification is most
legible before it spends to be understood somewhere new.
`cac_usd` is the fully-loaded cost of acquiring ONE paying
learner in that market — advertising, content, the admissions
conversation and the consultation, divided by learners enrolled.
It is higher in the Gulf because the sale is longer and more
personal, and lower in West Africa because reach is cheaper and
the qualification is already understood there.

regions.name: Asia and the rest of the world

_: WHAT THE COLLEGE SPENDS TO BE FOUND, year by year, in total.
THE MODEL RUNS FORWARD FROM THIS, not backwards from a revenue
target. Enrolment is budget divided by the cost of acquiring a
learner, then capped by how many learners the College can
actually teach. That ordering is the difference between a plan
and a hope: it is impossible to produce a flattering number here
without either spending the money or hiring the instructors.
Year 1 is deliberately small. The College has no cohort, no
completion record and no alumni; money spent before there is
anything to point at buys enquiries that do not convert.

regional_weights_by_year._: How the budget divides across open markets each year. Weights for a market that has not opened are zero and the engine redistributes.

_: THE STAGES BETWEEN A STRANGER AND A MATRICULATED LEARNER.
The rates below are applied to the enquiries the acquisition
budget buys. They are stated as an explicit chain rather than as
one blended conversion figure, because a blended figure hides the
stage that is actually failing and cannot be managed.
`consultation_to_application` is high because the consultation is
where placement happens: a person who has had the conversation
and been placed at a level has already chosen. `offer_to_paid` is
the hardest step in the chain and is modelled as such.
WHAT HAPPENS AFTER SOMEBODY PAYS, which is where most education
financial models quietly assume perfection.
`level_completion` is the share of learners who finish a level
they started. `continues_to_next` is the share of those who then
enrol on the following level. The two compound: at the rates
below, roughly a third of learners who begin Level I reach
Level VI, which is a defensible figure for a 24-month part-time
qualification and is far from the 100% an unexamined model
assumes.
Continuation rises with level because a learner who has completed
three levels has demonstrated they will complete a fourth. That
is the single most valuable fact in the whole commercial model
and it is why retention spending outperforms acquisition spending
from Year 4 onward.
THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS A MODEL RATHER THAN A CURVE.
Teaching is 36 per cent of a level fee and it is a named person:
written feedback on every produced piece, tutorials on request,
and academic responsibility for the level. That person can carry
a finite number of learners, and the model refuses to enrol more
learners in a year than the instructors hired that year can
teach. Revenue the College could not deliver is not revenue.
`learners_per_instructor` is concurrent, not annual.
_learners_per_instructor: NOT ASSERTED — DERIVED, and the derivation is the point.
The first draft of this plan asserted 48 learners per instructor.
The model then spent 19.4 per cent of net tuition on instruction
while data/tuition.json promises 36 per cent of every fee to
'Teaching and academic supervision — a named instructor, written
feedback on every piece of produced work, and tutorial time on
request'. A plan that charges for a named instructor at 36 per
cent and staffs at 19 is not an efficient plan; it is a plan that
does not intend to keep the promise printed on its own fee page.
The engine now computes the figure from the published teaching
allocation and the pace at which learners actually complete
levels, so the establishment cannot drift away from what the fee
says it buys. tests/masterplan.test.mjs fails the build if the
modelled instruction spend departs from the published share.

staffing._: Non-teaching establishment. Each role is a real post with a real salary, and the model hires them against thresholds rather than as a percentage of revenue.

technology_usd._: Platform, hosting, authentication, storage, media and security. Grows with active learners but not linearly — the architecture is serverless and the marginal cost of one more learner is small. The floor is what it costs to run the platform at all.

operating_usd._: Legal, accounting, insurance, audit, professional services, the London registered office and institutional administration.

_: THE LINE MOST PLANS LEAVE OUT, and the one this College cannot.
Publishing, the External Examiner, accreditation work, academic
research and international partnership development. It is funded
as a share of net tuition rather than from surplus, because a
line funded from surplus is a line that is cut in the year it is
most needed.
WHAT THE COLLEGE KEEPS, and the rule it keeps it by.
The target is stated in MONTHS OF OPERATING COST rather than as a
percentage of revenue, because the thing a reserve has to survive
is a year when revenue falls and cost does not. A percentage-of-
revenue reserve shrinks exactly when it is needed.
THREE FUTURES, DIFFERING IN STRUCTURE RATHER THAN IN OPTIMISM.
A scenario set whose only variable is 'more students' tests
nothing. Each of these changes something the College would
actually have to do differently: what it costs to be found, how
many learners stay, and what share of enrolment arrives through a
sponsoring institution rather than one at a time.

sensitivity._: Each is a single-variable shock applied to the expected case, so the effect of one thing can be read without another moving underneath it.

cases.label: Refunds at twice the modelled rate

_: MANAGEMENT'S PROPOSED COMMERCIAL ARCHITECTURE — PROPOSED, NOT ADOPTED.
Every figure in this block is a management proposal. None has been
adopted, none is published, and none may be presented as the
College's price until the Board resolves on it. The adopted tariff
remains $19,000 in data/tuition.json and on /admissions/tuition/
until that happens.
THIS BLOCK IS THE SECOND VERSION. THE FIRST DID NOT SURVIVE.
An earlier draft of this plan proposed $8,900 directed, $18,500
tutored and $34,000 / $58,000 / $96,000 executive, and projected
$61.6M of ten-year revenue on $14.1M of surplus. Those prices were
derived from a demand model whose willingness-to-pay figures were
asserted rather than researched.
They were then tested against real published prices — see
data/market-evidence.json, which records every observation with its
provider, its local price, the hours it buys and its source. The
researched willingness to pay came in materially below the assumed
figures in every segment: the Gulf executive at $24,000 rather than
$31,000, the Gulf professional at $13,000 rather than $17,500, the
UK and European buyer at $15,500 rather than $19,500, and West
Africa at $2,200 rather than $6,400 — a third of what the first
model assumed, and the correction that mattered most.
The $61.6M / $14.1M plan did not survive that test and is not
defended. It is recorded here because a plan that quietly replaces
its own numbers has told the Board nothing.
HOW THE PROPOSED PRICE WAS ARRIVED AT
Not by adjusting an existing number. scripts/publication/pricing.mjs
computes what each product costs to deliver — tutorial hours, group
hours at their real group size, pieces of produced work at the hours
they take to read, assessment, second marking, moderation and adviser
time, each weighted by the level, because a C2 script is not an A1
script. It then models what each market will pay, on the researched
figures, and lets the optimum land where it lands.
THE OPTIMISER'S OWN ANSWER WAS REJECTED BY MANAGEMENT. Unconstrained
surplus maximisation says: serve about 1,500 Gulf executives at the
boutique price and let the rest of the world go. That is a real
result of the arithmetic and it is the wrong institution — a few
hundred learners a year reaching C2 is a consultancy with a
syllabus, not a college. The Board is asked to note that the
proposal below deliberately forgoes surplus the model says is
available.
WHAT THE PROPOSAL COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS
Against the adopted flat $19,000, over ten years, the proposal earns
MORE revenue and LESS surplus. It admits roughly 12,600 learners
against 4,500, confers several times the awards, and ends the decade
with about 10,500 award-holders rather than about 3,700. The surplus
given up is the price of that reach, and management recommends it on
two grounds: alumni lower the cost of every later acquisition, so
the comparison narrows every year beyond the decade; and an
institution is measured by what it confers.
The Board may legitimately prefer the smaller, more profitable
College. That is a decision about what WEC-LC is for, not a
calculation, and the plan does not pretend the arithmetic settles
it.
WHAT THE PROPOSAL DOES NOT FIX
The Core case reaches cumulative break-even in the eighth year and
ends the decade a little above water. It is solvent and it is thin,
and its fragility is not in the price. Acquisition cost 40 per cent
above plan, or continuation ten per cent weaker, each turns the
decade negative. Neither figure has been researched. They are the
two assumptions the Board should interrogate hardest, and they are
worth more than any further movement in the tariff.
THE CONSTRAINT THAT SETS THE DIRECTED PRICE.
The pre-validation draft justified its Directed price on the
ground that revenue was flat above it. On researched demand that
is false: revenue and surplus both continue to rise well past it.
The reason is that a buyer priced out of Directed does not leave.
They step down to the adopted Independent route and sit the same
examinations for the same award without ever being taught. The
number of people the College CREDENTIALS barely moves across the
whole price range. What moves is whether it TEACHES them.
Unconstrained, the model puts Directed near $15,000, earns roughly
$2M more across the decade than the proposal does, and leaves
the College teaching 46 per cent of its candidates rather than
60. That is an examination board with a
syllabus attached, and it is the second time the optimiser has
proposed dissolving the institution in order to improve it.
So management proposes a stated institutional constraint instead.
The Board resolves on the SHARE; the price follows from it. The
frontier is published in the plan so the choice can be made on
evidence, and scripts/publication/pricing.mjs recomputes the
price from the share on every build — tests/masterplan.test.mjs
fails if the two ever drift apart.
teaching_majority._frontier_prices_usd: The Directed prices the published frontier is evaluated at. They live here rather than in the renderer so that no financial figure is typed into a page — tests/masterplan.test.mjs enforces that. The proposed price is inserted automatically and need not be listed.

_: A FINDING THE BOARD MUST BE GIVEN, not a number to bury.
data/masterplan.json § reserve sets the target at nine months of
operating cost. Under the proposed architecture, on validated
demand, NO PRICE IN THE RANGE TESTED reaches that target inside
the ten years — not the proposed price, and not the price that
maximises surplus. At Year 10 the Core case holds roughly $2.2M
against a target near $4.2M.
This is not an argument for charging more: raising Directed to
$12,000 still only reaches about $3.0M, and costs the teaching
majority to get there. It is a statement that a College of this
scale cannot fund nine months of cover out of a first decade's
trading, and that the Board has three options rather than one —
a founding capital contribution, a longer horizon to full
reserve, or a lower target. The plan does not choose among them.

proposed_architecture._committed_pathway_usd: Independent is NOT a proposal. $600 a level is adopted and published in data/commercial.json; it is listed here so the tariff can be read as a whole.

superseded_pathway_usd._: The pre-validation proposal, retained so the revision is visible.
superseded_pathway_usd.why_withdrawn: Its demand assumptions were asserted. Researched willingness to pay came in below them in every segment.

proposed_architecture.margin_disclosure: The Independent route — $600 a level, adopted and published — returns a gross margin of about 40 per cent once it carries its full share of institutional serving cost, below the 45 per cent management applies to the prices it is proposing. It is retained at that margin deliberately: it is the only route into a WEC-LC qualification that does not require tuition to be bought, it clears its own delivery and acquisition cost, and withdrawing or repricing it to meet an internal margin standard would close the College's cheapest door on its widest market.
proposed_architecture._frontier: The boundary figures the analysis produced, recorded here so the published plan can cite them rather than restate them. `boutique_price_usd` is where unconstrained surplus maximisation lands; `revenue_plateau_usd` is where revenue stops improving with price; `institutional_floor_usd` is the Directed price below which the decade never closes in surplus at all — found by bisection on the projection rather than asserted, and re-derived by tests/masterplan.test.mjs. The boutique and plateau figures moved down on researched demand, and the plateau ARGUMENT was withdrawn entirely; see teaching_majority.

fragility._: Single-variable shocks to the Core case, from scripts/publication/projection.mjs. Recorded so the published plan cites them rather than restating them.
fragility.binding_constraint_note: At validated demand the College spends about $1.8M of a $2.76M Year 10 acquisition budget. What limits enrolment is not money but the number of people it can put a considered proposition in front of — and that figure is modelled, never researched.

proposed_architecture.basis: scripts/publication/pricing.mjs — delivery cost computed hour by hour; demand modelled per segment with elasticity and a credibility floor, on the willingness-to-pay figures in data/market-evidence.json.
proposed_architecture.supersedes_nothing: The adopted tariff in data/tuition.json is unchanged and remains the published price.

_: THE COMMISSIONING BRIEF'S ARCHITECTURE, modelled rather than
dismissed: ten levels of 120 hours, sold as a directed pathway at
$7,400 and a tutored pathway at $14,800, against the adopted six
levels of 200 hours at $19,000.
The Three Architectures section computes what adopting it would do.
The figures here are its inputs, not a recommendation.
